summary: Reviewed CoverImageViewModel.cs and CoverImageViewModelTests.cs against all four Review Dimensions.

Maintainability: Well-structured ViewModel. Visual section separators aid navigation. DisposeAndClearBitmap and SetPreviewFromBytes helpers keep command methods clean. RotateCcw correctly uses (RotationDegrees + 270) % 360 as the mathematical equivalent of -90 mod 360. DisposeAndClearBitmap follows the same dispose-before-null pattern as ThumbnailItemViewModel.

Best Practices: [RelayCommand(CanExecute = nameof(CanApply))] + [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor] on HasCoverImage is idiomatic. ApplyNow correctly bakes rotation into the file then resets RotationDegrees to 0. OnCoverImageUpdated() provides a clean external reload entry point.

Fix-Forward applied: SetPreviewFromBytes now uses `using var ms = new MemoryStream(bytes)`. Avalonia reads the stream eagerly so disposal is safe immediately after Bitmap construction. Behaviorally identical — QA validation remains intact.
No Blocking issues found.

comments.note: reviewer-applied-fix: Added `using var ms` in SetPreviewFromBytes. Avalonia's Bitmap constructor reads the stream eagerly and synchronously, so the MemoryStream can be disposed immediately after. The original code left the MemoryStream unreferenced (relying on GC). While MemoryStream backed by a byte[] has no unmanaged resources, the explicit using block is cleaner and consistent with RefreshRotationPreviewAsync which already uses local variables for the stream.

CoverImageViewModel does not implement IDisposable. PreviewBitmap (Avalonia Bitmap — a native resource) will not be released until GC collects the ViewModel. For a dialog-lifetime ViewModel opened infrequently this is acceptable, but future work should consider adding IDisposable to release PreviewBitmap deterministically when the dialog closes.
